title: Angular momentum
examples: What is the formula for angular momentum?
How does mass affect angular momentum?
Can angular momentum be conserved in real life?

explain.say: Today we learn about angular momentum in rotation.
Angular momentum L is found by multiplying moment of inertia I by angular speed ω.

items: L is the value | Iω is the calculation

explain.say: The principle of conservation means angular momentum stays constant.
An ice skater spinning slowly has high angular momentum.
When the skater pulls arms in, moment of inertia I decreases greatly.
In everyday life, a spinning top conserves its angular momentum.

faq.q: What is the difference between angular momentum and linear momentum?
faq.a: Linear momentum involves straight-line motion, while angular momentum involves rotational motion. Both are measures of inertia in their respective directions.
asks: Is angular momentum related to straight lines?

faq.q: Does conservation of angular momentum mean the object stops spinning?
faq.a: No, it means the product I times ω remains the same if no external torque acts. It can change the speed, not necessarily stop the spin.
asks: If L is conserved, does it mean nothing changes?

faq.q: What causes the moment of inertia I?
faq.a: The moment of inertia depends on how the mass is distributed relative to the axis of rotation. More spread out mass means larger I.
asks: Does distance from axis affect I?
What determines the moment of inertia?

faq.q: Can I use this law when something is speeding up?
faq.a: You can use it if the net external torque acting on the system is zero. If there is a torque, angular momentum is not conserved.
asks: When is angular momentum not conserved?
What needs to be zero for conservation?

faq.q: Why does the ice skater spin faster when pulling their arms in?
faq.a: Pulling the arms in decreases the moment of inertia I. To keep L constant, the angular speed ω must increase.
asks: Why does I change when the skater moves?
What happens to ω if I gets smaller?

facts: Angular momentum L is a vector quantity.
The formula is L equals moment of inertia times angular speed.
Conservation applies when the net external torque is zero.
Moment of inertia depends on mass distribution.

quiz.say: A spinning wheel slows down because air resistance creates a torque. What happens to its angular momentum?
quiz.why: Air resistance creates a torque, meaning the system is not isolated, so L is not conserved.

wrong.0: This is wrong because air resistance applies a torque, which changes the angular momentum.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the wheel might slow down but not stop completely.
wrong.2: This is wrong because air resistance always opposes the motion, causing a decrease.

quiz.say: If the moment of inertia I is doubled and the angular speed ω is halved, what is the new angular momentum L?
quiz.why: Since L = Iω, doubling I and halving ω results in the product remaining unchanged.

wrong.1: This incorrectly assumes that only the angular speed determines the final momentum.
wrong.2: This incorrectly assumes that only the moment of inertia determines the final momentum.
wrong.3: This incorrectly multiplies the changes in both I and ω.

quiz.say: A figure skater pulls their arms in rapidly. Which statement correctly describes the change in L?

options.show: L depends only on the final speed
options.say: L depends only on the final speed

options.show: L increases because they spin faster
options.say: L increases because they spin faster

quiz.why: Since there are no external torques, the angular momentum must be conserved during the spin.

wrong.0: L depends on both the moment of inertia and the angular speed.
wrong.2: While ω increases, L must remain constant if no external torque acts.
wrong.3: This ignores the conservation principle that dictates L must stay the same.
